宅男神游闪乱神乐系列的第二部，这代并没有像前作爆裂那样有重置，也不像后代选择那么新，这代就是从psv直接移植过来的，所以硬性缺点很多，前提先说明只推荐给阿宅粉丝和闪乱神乐系列的粉丝。

先说缺点，首先我也说了是psv老游戏移植了，pc适配度特别烂！！！这个游戏只推荐手柄玩。其次，游戏里充满各种日本老游戏繁琐的UI设计，刚开始玩经常为了找一个东西在UI界面到处来回找。最后就是没有中文，不过还好有补丁，我连着去圣光补丁一起打的，能用，就是偶尔有小bug，不算特别严重。

然后就是优点，首先，这一代里的角色，玩起来战斗系统竟然比爆裂还舒服，上一代很肉很慢的手感，在这一代竟然没有，手感更快。而且剧情比爆裂也是要丰富的，这一代四个学校都有剧情，而且还给每个人都做了单独的小格外剧情，有的很好玩。最后当然就是福利了，宅味浓度极高，不过角色们变身动作没爆裂那么丰富，而且还有我最喜欢的，[spoiler] 角色们奶子都很大.
 [/spoiler]

虽然闪乱神乐SV以现在看不是一款很好的游戏，不过对于喜欢老宅文化的老宅男们来说，这确实是很有“那个年代二次元味道”的游戏，现在这种老派宅游越来越少了，不过闪乱神乐还是值得一玩的，推荐！

Senran Kagura: Shinovi Versus sabe exatamente qual é o seu público e não tenta esconder isso. Se ignorar ou aceitar o foco exagerado em fanservice, dá pra encontrar um título competente por baixo dessa camada.

A história é dividida entre diferentes escolas, cada uma com seu próprio grupo de personagens e conflitos. É uma trama simples, mas bem resolvida, resultando em uma história boa no geral. Um ponto interessante é que você joga a campanha de cada uma das quatro escolas, o que permite ver os acontecimentos por perspectivas diferentes. Inclusive, é até meio surpreendente ver que o jogo tenta trabalhar alguns momentos mais sérios. Não é nada incrível, mas considerando que a expectativa inicial pode ser praticamente zero história, essa profundidade acaba sendo um ponto positivo.

Na jogabilidade, ele segue o estilo musou, que seria você contra vários inimigos ao mesmo tempo, e seu arsenal sendo composto com vários ataques devastadores. Ele foca no básico que funciona e é, principalmente, divertido. A parte técnica é modesta e cumpre bem o que se propõe.

No geral, é um jogo bacana. Ele se mantém em um nível equilibrado, entregando uma experiência sólida sem cometer erros graves. Só que é importante deixar claro que, se o estilo visual e o fanservice te incomodam, dificilmente dá pra aproveitar o resto. Caso contrário, dá pra se divertir um pouquinho.

[Na jornada da platina da franquia Senran Kagura][PT-3]


Olha, eu não vou mentir, esse aqui foi mais difícil de descer do que os dois jogos anteriores que eu joguei. Pouco contexto para começar uma análise? Pois bem, após jogar Burst Renew, o remake do primeiro jogo da série, e ver o quão foi divertido platina-lo, eu decidi fazer o mesmo com todos os jogos da franquia. Sair do Burst Renew para o Estival Versus já mostrou que houveram muitas mudanças de um jogo pra outro, apesar de em sua maioria visuais, e acabou que o ritmo de Estival Versus foi até melhor que o BR. Porém, Shinovi Versus é bem diferente.

Esse foi o primeiro Senran Kagura a vir para o PC e o segundo jogo da série (Apesar de existir um Senran Kagura II que na verdade é o terceiro), originalmente um jogo de PS Vita, a diferença de gameplay entre ele e os jogos mais modernos que joguei anteriormente (Burst Renew e Estival Versus) é bem grande. Eu imagino que se tratando do PS Vita esse jogo deva ser divertidíssimo de se jogar no portátil, mas quando colocado em comparação aos que vieram depois é um pouco duro de não sentir que esse é mais pesado e lento.

De qualquer forma, eu gosto de pensar no jogo independente de seus sucessores, em como seria joga-lo na época em que ele saiu, sem já ter a experiência dos mais recentes. Nesse aspecto eu ainda acho que Shinovi Versus é bem solido, um solido mediano. Sobre a historia... eu realmente não me lembro de basicamente nada do que está acontecendo aqui (É, mais um que eu pulei tudo), mas já temos todas as 3 academias e o esquadrão da Homura que se desvincula de seu colégio ninja após o final do primeiro jogo.

Sim, você vai sentir que esse aqui talvez não tenha envelhecido tão bem, mas está longe de ser um jogo ruim, é um jogo de portátil com suas limitações, mas que se segura bem.

Senran Kagura: Shinobi Versus is a mixed bag when compared to Senran Kagura: Burst Renewal. Before I begin, it’s best to mentioned that I have pasted my review of Burst Renewal at the end of this review for added context. With that said, set’s start with with the bad in Shinobi Versus;  
1. The visual indicators are much fainter and subtle, in some cases disappearing entirely. The yellow and purple indicators for attacks that can or cannot be parried are gone, and the green ring for when to chase an opponent is fainter. You’ll just have to guess what’s what in this game, which is a definite minus. Of course, opinions will differ, but Walt Disney’s Laws of Animation also strongly apply to gaming, especially the laws of anticipation and clarity. The more a player is able to anticipate and know what’s going on the better their ability to react and engage with the game in a way they find satisfying.  

2. The ability of a player to retry a battle after losing is severely hampered by being forced to go through the experience and summary screen. As someone who had to retry some battles several times in succession, I found this incredibly irritating.  

And now on to the good  
1. The home area is much improved compared to Burst Renewal and the menu that can be brought up if you’d rather not wander around is a definite plus.  

2. The combat is faster and feels more engaging and demanding of your attention, this part is a definite plus, but it’s sadly hampered by the reduced visual clarity of enemy type of attack mentioned prior. While those with mastery over the mechanics from the prior game might not be overly impacted, it would definitely have made for better gameplay to keep those indicators in.  

3. Another school has been added, bringing the total number of schools in Shinobi Versus to 3 as opposed to 2. This means more gameplay, and more eye candy and visual research.  

4. The fan service has been massively, distinctly improved. Better angles and animations both for Shinobi Transformation and clothing destruction, more deliberately seductive motions for clothing destruction, and MORE clothing destruction. The developers are men of, no, NOBILITY OF CULTURE with the heroic hearts who insist on top tier visual research for their target audience. Add mods, and boys, we are in heaven. I often see people say "I came for the lewds but stayed for the gameplay" to which I usually call ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. This game makes me want to say that very same thing. Senran Kagura is a spectacle hack n slash game, so it happens to be in my favortie action game genre, but the game is also famed for the fanservice, and boy oh boy, I can't praise this game enough. If you're fan of fanservice, general lewdness and hack n slash games, this game is a dream come true.

The hack n slash combo mechanics are definitely not in the league of Ninja Gaiden or Devil May Cry, but it's still structured in a way that demands your attention, so while it's button-mashy compared to the aforementioned games, you still have to pay close attention to the visual cues to make sure you chase, parry, block, and dodge when you need to. Underlying it all is clothing destruction and sexy transformations that add eye-candy and constantly tease you. Best of all, if you want more spice, you can enhance your experience with mods to change the clothing to your taste, or banish them from obstructing your... visual research.

Overall, a hack n slash game that uniquely manages to be engaging and relaxing at the same time, feelings very satisfying to play. For the those interested, the story is also surprisingly deep and worthwhile to experience. 8.9/10 - 9/10 without mods. 9.5/10 - 9.8/10 with mods, an absolute must-play. Cheers!!! Новогоднее похмелье проходит, а знакомство с серией Senran Kagura продолжается.

Shinovi Versus - это, по сути, сиквел Burst, и события стартуют примерно через полгода после финальной битвы с ебакой в Академии Хебидзе. Первое, что бросится в глаза - это то, что каст активных в истории персонажей расширился; так, вместо двух сюжеток игроку предложат аж четыре кампании, где у каждой из 5-6 героинь еще и своя бонусная индивидуальная история. То есть около 200 коротких миссий с текстовыми перебивками. 

История будет крутиться вокруг Королевской Битвы Шиноби (школа против школы, условно); при этом, по ходу повествования пробрасывается истинная суть борьбы между добрыми и злыми чуваками (и, как понимаю, эта тема и дальше будет центральным сюжетом, плюс-минус). Собственно, несмотря на некоторые различия и противоречия, первый три кампании как раз и покажут вам эту межуниверситетскую специальную олимпиаду по боевому раздеванию оппонентов; четвертая история уже пойдет навстречу к главгаду.

В отличии от Burst ReNewal, SKSV - это чистый порт, без наворотов, апгрейдов графики и прочего (ну, почти). На каких-нибудь скидках за копейки вы покупаете сразу полную игру, без DLC и прочих непотребств, которые раздувают даже на распродажах финальный ценник игр серии до безбожных значений (да, у меня все еще травма от попыток в несколько заходов закупить DLC для Peach Beach Splash).

А еще, учитывая минимум изменений, здесь и старая боевка. С одной стороны, она ощущается менее удобной; с другой, общая простота боевой системы перекрывается разнообразием персонажей и тем, что они обрели еще больше индивидуальности в плане поведения в драке. Хомура, к примеру, теперь может включить рыжую форму и безнаказанно несколько секунд избивать врагов; Хикаге тоже вместо второго спецприема переходит в другую стойку и шинкует заточкой полки врагов за секунды. В общем, все это динамично и весело. 

Отдельно, кстати, стоит отметить наличие мультиплеера. Погонять с людьми не удалось, но его присутствие повлияло на сингловый режим: теперь у героинь всегда те же атаки как под вашим контролем, так и на позиции босса по управлением ИИ (уникальные босс-мувсеты в первой части немного раздражали). Это не делает бои фундаментально проще, впрочем; ИИ-оппонент может лихо вжать в угол и не дать из него выйти. Зато одинаковый инструментарий в бою теперь может привести к воздушному столкновению - бешеному QTE, где нужно перекликать супостата и оглушить его. Естественно, с учетом этого в игре, по моим ощущениям, в бою против девушек-ниндзя резко подскакивает полезность такого приема, как парирование, потому что именно оно может оглушить, отбросить и открыть для ответного комбо обнаглевшего соперника.

Остальные отличия - больше косметические. Гача с трусами, интерактивный хаб у каждого отряда вместо обычного меню, немного другая кастомизация и взаимодействие с барышнями в гардеробной...

Но в целом я более чем доволен. Игра мало стоит, мало требует, но сразу четко дает понять, что не относится к самой себе слишком серьезно. Люди тут за битвами до последнего исподнего, а не за драмой или сложными механиками. Ну и ради вайфу-гейминга! :)  А еще это игра, напоминающая о тех временах, когда внутриигровой контент мы не покупали, а открывали и зарабатывали своими ручками, эх... Хоть и фраза про "заработать ручками" в отзыве на игру серии Senran Kagura и выглядит более двусмысленно, чем я это задумывал xD

I actually played Senran Kagura Shinovi Versus back on PSVita years ago, finished it completely, and now that I am replaying it on a much more powerful PC, it honestly feels like experiencing the game the way it was always meant to be played.

If you like stylish anime action games that are honest about being fun, flashy, and fan service-heavy, this one is absolutely worth it.

[h1]Senran Kagura Shinovi Versus (Steam)[/h1]
[b]Recomendación:[/b] Sí, especialmente en oferta

[hr]

[h2]Una entrega clásica de la saga adaptada a PC con bastante contenido[/h2]
Senran Kagura Shinovi Versus fue originalmente un título portátil, pero su adaptación a Steam mantiene la esencia de la saga: acción rápida, humor absurdo, fanservice y una cantidad considerable de contenido.
Es de las entregas que sentaron la base del estilo moderno del hack & slash de Senran Kagura.

Aunque se siente más “simple” que Estival Versus o Burst Re:Newal, sigue siendo sólido en gameplay y sorprendentemente entretenido por la cantidad de personajes jugables y las mini campañas de cada uno.

[hr]

[h2]Jugabilidad y mecánicas[/h2]
• Combate hack & slash directo y fluido
• Movilidad rápida con saltos, esquivas y cancelaciones
• Transformaciones que aumentan daño y opciones de combate
• Finalizaciones con pequeñas cinemáticas si rematas correctamente
• Misiones por personaje que dan variedad
• Buen número de enemigos por pantalla con patrones distintos
• Personalización amplia: trajes, accesorios y colores
• Progresión constante con recompensas regulares

La jugabilidad es menos técnica que en entregas posteriores, pero eso no la hace peor: es más sencilla, más arcade y más inmediata. Ideal si buscas batallas rápidas y sin complicaciones.

[hr]

[h2]Historia, personajes y presentación[/h2]
El juego ofrece varias rutas según cada escuela y combina el humor típico de la saga con fragmentos más serios. No es una historia profunda, pero funciona bien dentro del tono del juego.

Los personajes son muchos y cada casa tiene su propio lore, lo cual mantiene el interés aunque las misiones repitan estructura.

Gráficamente se nota su origen portátil:
• Modelos decentes, pero simples
• Escenarios limitados pero aceptables
• Expresiones faciales algo rígidas
• Buen uso de efectos y transformaciones

Las cinemáticas estilo novela visual cumplen y los retratos 2D están bien trabajados para su época.

La banda sonora es adecuada y acompaña bien las peleas.

[hr]

[h2]Puntos débiles[/h2]
• Se nota que viene de una consola portátil: escenarios y animaciones simples
• La IA es irregular: a veces muy pasiva, a veces te lanza combos de la nada
• Algunas misiones pueden sentirse repetitivas
• Si vienes de Estival Versus, Shinovi te va a parecer más limitado técnicamente
• Modo online prácticamente inexistente hoy en día

[hr]

[h2]Conclusión[/h2]
Shinovi Versus es una pieza importante dentro de la saga: divertido, rápido y con un ritmo arcade que lo hace ideal para sesiones cortas o para avanzar poco a poco.
Tiene bastante contenido para ser un título portátil adaptado, mantiene una buena variedad de personajes y su estilo hack & slash es simple pero efectivo.

[b]Recomendado en oferta.[/b]
Vale la pena si te gusta la franquicia o el género, pero hay que tener claro que fue un juego de Vita y eso se nota en lo técnico. Aun así, cumple bien y sigue siendo muy entretenido.

If you’re easily offended, maybe skip it. But if you’re looking for an absurdly fun brawler that knows exactly what it is and doesn’t care — welcome to paradise, my fellow shinobi.

"Listen… I didn’t come here for deep storytelling — I came here for ninja battles, flashy attacks, and pure chaos. And on that front, this game delivered exactly what I wanted."

Senran Kagura Shinovi Versus, developed by Tamsoft and published by XSEED Games and Marvelous, is an unapologetically over-the-top brawler that combines fast-paced, anime-inspired combat with an unmistakably provocative aesthetic. Originally released on the PlayStation Vita before making its way to PC, it stands as one of the most defining entries in the Senran Kagura franchise—an eccentric series that embraces absurdity, charm, and chaos in equal measure. The game doesn’t shy away from its identity; it’s a mixture of genuine mechanical fun and tongue-in-cheek fanservice, offering something both playful and self-aware. Beneath the skimpy outfits and comical exaggerations lies a surprisingly robust beat-’em-up that succeeds at being entertaining, even if it’s not particularly deep.

The narrative framework of Shinovi Versus revolves around four rival shinobi academies, each with its own roster of female warriors. Every school has its ideology and backstory, creating a web of rivalries that drive the game’s campaign. The structure is segmented into four main storylines, one for each faction, and each tells its own version of events through a blend of visual novel-style dialogue sequences and explosive battles. While the story often dips into melodrama and comedy, it also carries moments of genuine character development, exploring the girls’ aspirations, rivalries, and loyalties. The writing is lighthearted, with a heavy dose of self-awareness, and though it never takes itself too seriously, it manages to make each character memorable through humor and exaggerated emotion.

Combat is the centerpiece, and it captures the essence of a fast, fluid, and accessible brawler. Each character has a distinct fighting style, weapon type, and set of combos, ensuring variety across the 20-plus playable fighters. Battles unfold in open 3D arenas where players string together light and heavy attacks, air juggles, and special moves to overwhelm waves of enemies or duel against rival shinobi. The controls are smooth and responsive, making it easy for newcomers to enjoy while offering enough depth for more experienced players to experiment with different characters. Transformations—activated mid-battle through a burst of energy—grant temporary stat boosts and new moves, while the “clothing destruction” system doubles as both a gameplay indicator and a trademark feature of the series. As the fight progresses, characters’ outfits tear away with each hit, serving as a mix of comedy and spectacle that defines the series’ irreverent tone.

Visually, Shinovi Versus benefits from its transition to PC. The higher resolution, stable frame rate, and cleaner textures make the colorful character models stand out far better than on its handheld origins. Each fighter is meticulously detailed, with fluid animations that highlight the game’s kinetic energy. The environments, while limited in variety, are bright and serve as fitting backdrops for the action. The camera occasionally struggles to keep up with the chaos, especially during crowded fights, but it rarely detracts from the overall flow. The soundtrack reinforces the game’s personality—a mix of upbeat electronic battle themes and traditional Japanese motifs that perfectly match the mixture of comedy and intensity that defines the experience.

While Shinovi Versus offers a satisfying burst of fun in short sessions, it’s not without repetition. The mission design, though energetic, often follows the same pattern: fight groups of enemies, face a rival shinobi, watch a cutscene, and repeat. The variety lies primarily in the characters rather than in the objectives or level design. However, the large cast and their individualized move sets help to keep things fresh for players who enjoy experimenting. The game also includes multiplayer, allowing up to four players to battle online or locally, though the online community has dwindled over time. When active, multiplayer matches add an exciting layer of unpredictability, as players clash in frantic free-for-alls filled with special attacks and comedic chaos.

Tonally, Shinovi Versus is as polarizing as it is distinctive. Its unabashed embrace of fanservice—complete with exaggerated character designs, suggestive humor, and playful innuendo—sets it apart from more conventional action games. This aspect is central to its appeal but also the reason it alienates some players. For those who approach it with an understanding of its over-the-top intent, it becomes clear that the game isn’t trying to shock but to celebrate its absurdity. The developers lean into the humor, balancing the sexualized imagery with genuine warmth and camaraderie among the characters. It’s a game that thrives on contradiction—equal parts silly and sincere, ridiculous and surprisingly heartfelt.

Despite its flaws, Shinovi Versus succeeds because it knows exactly what it wants to be. It’s not a technical masterpiece or a deeply strategic fighter, but it’s fast, flashy, and unashamedly fun. The blend of anime aesthetics, accessible combat, and playful tone creates a distinct experience that’s hard to find elsewhere. For fans of the Senran Kagura series, it represents a high point in terms of both content and personality. For newcomers, it serves as an entry point into a world that doesn’t take itself too seriously but still offers genuine entertainment.

In the end, Senran Kagura Shinovi Versus is a game of excess—of action, energy, and attitude. It celebrates style over subtlety, and in doing so, crafts a uniquely enjoyable, if divisive, experience. It’s a title that revels in its absurdity while still delivering a satisfying combat system that rewards fast reactions and experimentation. For those willing to embrace its eccentricity, it provides a surprisingly polished and enjoyable action romp filled with humor, charm, and relentless energy. It may not appeal to everyone, but it remains a confident, unapologetic entry in the anime brawler genre, defined as much by its outrageous personality as by the fun at its core.
